deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page belongs to Gauss's 1807 work on the orbit of PALLAS, not Ceres. Two clues fix this. The latitudes are about +46°, -54° and +42°, and the inclination found is 34°37'. The planet symbol transcribed as ⚳ is therefore Pallas (⚴).

PART A. Reducing one observation to the 1807 opposition.

(1) Time of observation. Milan ('Mayland') time 14h32'16", minus the Milan–Paris longitude difference 27'25", gives 14h4'49" Paris mean time. The line written as 'May 15. 2h32'16"' is most likely 'May 4. 14h32'16"'; the reasons are given at step (8).

(2) Solar theory (tables with arguments A, B, C, D, E, F, N).
- Mean longitude 1s12°0'44.4".
- Equation of centre +1°35'37.6".
- Perturbations: Moon 3.4", Venus 8.4", Mars 4.2", Jupiter 22.9", Saturn 0.5".
- A further +20.2". My interpretation: the tables have the aberration built into the epoch, and this term removes it to give the geometric place.
- Sum: Sun 43°37'21.6", so Earth's heliocentric longitude is 223°37'21.6".
- Radius vector: 1.0090963 + 0.0000673 (Moon) + 103 (Venus) + 145 + 296 + 24 (in units of the 7th decimal) = 1.0092204. Hence log R = 0.0039860.
- Sun's latitude from the terms A+B+N, 2B-C, 3C-4B, B-2E: +0.60 + 0.10 - 0.25 + 0.16 = +0.61". Earth's heliocentric latitude is therefore -0.61".

(3) Obliquity: 23°27'53.35" - 3.10" - 0.17" = 23°27'50.08" (true obliquity). Nutation in longitude is 17.10".

(4) Observed place from the ephemeris.
- Computed: α = 233°56'11.70", δ = +24°21'41.86".
- Errors (computed minus observed): +7.15" and -2.40".
- Observed: α = 233°56'4.55", δ = 24°21'44.26".

(5) Conversion α, δ → λ, β with auxiliary logarithms.
- Example: 9.6559322 - 9.9075970 = 9.7483352.
- Auxiliary angles 29°15'25.57" and 52°43'15.65".
- Result: apparent λ = 223°37'46.67".
- Removing nutation (-17.10"): λ = 223°37'29.57" (mean equinox), β = 42°11'25.07".

(6) Differential coefficients of (λ, β) with respect to (α, δ), using an auxiliary angle -18°26'38".
- log ∂λ/∂α = 0.06683
- log ∂λ/∂δ = 9.63043n
- log ∂β/∂α = 9.45970
- log ∂β/∂δ = 9.97710
These are applied to the daily geocentric motions: dα = -740.97"/d (log 2.86985n) and dδ = +552.4"/d (log 2.74221).
- dλ/dt = -864.34 - 235.85 = -1100.19"/day.
- dβ/dt = -213.575 + 523.975 = +310.40"/day.
- Also listed: Sun's daily motion 3485.12"/d (written '∂☉', transcribed '∂δ') and d log R = +1047 units of the 7th decimal per day.

(7) Instant of opposition (my reconstruction, numerically confirmed). At 14h4'49" the Sun+180° is 21.6" and the planet is at 29.57".
- Δt = 7.97" / (3485.12 + 1100.19) = 0.001738 d = 2m30s.
- Opposition: 1807 May 4, 14h7'19" Paris mean time.
- λ = 29.57 - 1100.19×0.001738 → 223°37'27.66".
- β = 25.07 + 310.40×0.001738 → 42°11'25.61".
- log R = 0.0039862; Sun's latitude -0.61".
Adding 33'35" (Seeberg minus Paris) gives 14h40'54", the time used in the table below.

(8) Why the date is May 4, 14h. These interpolations reproduce the boxed values exactly. That only works if the observation was at 14h4'49" Paris on May 4.

PART B. 'Bestimmung der Elemente der Pallas aus folgenden 4 Oppositionen.'

(9) The four oppositions, with times t in days from 1803 Jan 0:
- 1803 Jun 30: t = 181.021354
- 1804 Aug 30: t = 608.209491
- 1805 Nov 29: t = 1064.471030
- 1807 May 4: t = 1585.611736
- A further epoch: t = 2034.891076
Each line gives λ, β and log R.

(10) Precession at 50.10"/yr, log of daily rate 9.13725 (0.13717"/day):
- 181.02 d × 0.13717 = 24.83"
- 608.21 d → 83.43"
- 1064.47 d → 146.01"
- 1585.61 d → 217.50"
- 2034.89 d → 279.12"
The logs 2.25773, 2.78406, 3.02713, 3.20020 and 3.30854 are log t.

(11) Hypothesis: Ω(1803) = 172°28'56.80", i = 34°37'41.55". The node is carried with precession:
- 172°29'21.63"
- 172°30'20.23"
- 172°31'22.81"
- 172°32'34.30"

(12) At opposition the heliocentric longitude equals the geocentric one, so the longitudes λ - Ω are:
- 105°10'2.37"
- 164°30'15.83"
- 254°49'20.09"
- 51°4'53.40"
Argument of latitude, from tan u = tan(λ-Ω)/cos i:
- log tan(λ-Ω) = 0.5668998, 9.4428589, 0.5665869, 0.0928943
- log cos i = 9.9153242
- u = 102°34'28.63", 161°22'47.94", 257°24'59.79", 56°23'59.72"
Heliocentric latitude, from tan b = tan i · sin(λ-Ω):
- log sin(λ-Ω) = 9.9846020, 9.4267786, 9.9845805, 9.8910021
- log tan i = 9.8392144
- b = 33°41'4.00", 10°27'12.39", -33°40'59.29", 28°14'56.82"
The next page compares these with the observations ('Errores latt. heli.') and derives δi and δΩ.

(13) Hypothesis: aphelion 1803 at 301°3'10.47", φ = 14°10'58.94" (e = sin φ). The argument of perihelion is ω = 301°3'10.47" + 180° - Ω = 308°34'13.67".
True anomalies v = u - ω:
- 154°0'14.96"
- 212°48'34.27"
- 308°50'46.12"
- 107°49'46.05"

(14) Last row: |v - E| (true minus eccentric anomaly), from tan(E/2) = sqrt((1-e)/(1+e)) tan(v/2):
- 7°1'34.66"
- 8°36'37.0"
- 10°16'18.1"
- 14°2'16.77"
The next page then forms E, M = E - e sin E and the mean motion, and solves least-squares-type conditions for corrections x, y to aphelion and eccentricity.

This is Gauss's standard procedure (later Theoria Motus II.3) for correcting elements from several oppositions.
errors: Daily motion in longitude: the sum -864.34 - 235.85 equals -1100.19". The value transcribed as -1160.19 is either a misreading or a pen slip. The subsequent interpolation (−1.91" in λ over 2m30s) uses 1100.19, so the computation is correct.
λ - Ω for 1804: 337°0'36.10" - 172°30'20.23" = 164°30'15.87", but the page has 15.83". This is a 0.04" discrepancy and is negligible.
The v - E entry for 1804 reads 8°36'27.025" in the transcription. Recomputation, and the next page, give 8°36'37.0". This is either a misreading or a 10" slip that was corrected on the next page.
The 1805 v - E entry of 10°16'18.17" differs from the next page's 10°16'18.13" by 0.04". This is trivial.

results.what: Reduction of a meridian observation (Milan) to the instant and place of opposition of Pallas, 1807 May 4 14h7'19" Paris, λ = 223°37'27.66", β = 42°11'25.61". Uses the Sun's place from tables, nutation, conversion α, δ → λ, β, and differential coefficients for linear interpolation in time.
results.modern_name: Reduction of an observation to opposition (classical orbit-determination practice)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th/19th-century astronomical practice (Delambre, von Zach, Gauss)

results.what: Correction of Pallas elements from four oppositions (1803–1807). Steps: precessed node; reduction to the orbit plane via tan u = tan(λ-Ω)/cos i; heliocentric latitude via tan b = tan i sin(λ-Ω); true anomaly v = u - ω under the hypothesis aphelion 301°3'10" and φ = 14°10'59"; then eccentric anomaly.
results.modern_name: Differential correction of orbital elements from oppositions (Gauss's method of four oppositions; least-squares element improvement)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria Motus 1809; Pallas elements published in von Zach's Monatliche Correspondenz)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine working material from Gauss's well-documented 1807 Pallas orbit computations: reduction to opposition and element correction from four oppositions. The procedures and the results are known to be his and were partially published. The only details of interest are the exact bookkeeping (Seeberg time, opposition interpolation).

checkable.asserts: The daily motion in longitude is the sum of the two contributions, -1100.19" (not -1160.19).
∂λ/∂α times dα gives -864.34".
∂λ/∂δ (negative) times dδ gives -235.85".
∂β/∂α times dα gives -213.575".
∂β/∂δ times dδ gives 523.975".
The interval from observation (14h4m49s) to opposition (14h7m19s) is about 150 s.
The longitude interpolated to opposition is 223°37'27.66".
The latitude interpolated to opposition is 42°11'25.61".
log of the Sun's radius vector.
The radius vector is the sum of the tabular perturbations.
The Sun's latitude is +0.61".
True obliquity 23°27'50.08".
Precession amounts at 50.10"/yr for each epoch.
log of daily precession.
tan u = tan(λ-Ω)/cos i gives u = 102°34'28.63" for 1803. Here deg = 180/pi*x and rad = pi/180*x.
Heliocentric latitude for 1803 is 33°41'4".
Aphelion longitude = Ω + ω - 180°, i.e. ω = 308°34'13.67".

transcription_corrections: The planet symbol ⚳ (Ceres) should be ⚴ (Pallas). The latitudes (+46°, -54°) and inclination 34°37' are Pallas's.

'1807. May. 15. 2h 32' 16"' is almost certainly '1807 May 4. 14h32'16" in Mayland'. The Paris line should read '14h 4' 49"' (mislabelled '5 2. 4. 49'). The interpolation to the boxed opposition at 14h7'19" confirms this.
'∂λ - 1160,19' should be '-1100,19', which is the sum of -864.34 and -235.85.
'∂δ 3485.12' is most likely '∂☉ 3485.12', the Sun's daily motion in arc seconds.
In the bottom row, '7 11 34,66' should be '7° 1' 34"66'.
In the bottom row, '11 16 18 17' should be '10° 16' 18"17'.
In the bottom row, '8 36 27,025' is probably '8° 36' 37"025', matching the next page and recomputation.
'Hypothesis Aphel. 1803 301° 3'10"47' and '14.10.58,94' are, respectively, the aphelion longitude and the eccentricity angle φ (e = sin φ).
